title: Framework Agreement for Minor Highway Works (Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council and Test Valley Borough Council)
description:
Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council in partnership with Test Valley Borough Council are seeking expressions of interest from relevant suppliers to tender for their Framework Contract for Minor Highway Works. Please note that this Framework contract covers the Borough of Basingstoke and Deane and the Borough of Test Valley, both in Hampshire.\\\\r\\r\r
\\\\r\\r\r
The contract will operate for a period of 3 years with a 1 year option to extend, and is expected to commence from 01/09/2019 and cover Highway Civil Engineering projects ranging anywhere from a few hundred pounds up to £75,000.00.\\\\r\\r\r
\\\\r\\r\r
Typical works let through this contract are of a Highway Civil Engineering nature and range from the construction of drop kerbs and small footway links to the implementation of additional parking projects and neighbourhood regeneration schemes.  Any one project could comprise elements of traffic management, site clearance, fencing, drainage, earthworks, kerbing, macadam surfacing and / or street furniture installation; hence suitable bidders will be those with experience of all of these areas.\\\\r\\r\r
\\\\r\\r\r
This Framework contract comprises submitted rates against each individual item listed within the Contract Schedule of Items. Bidders must be able to supply every item listed within Document 5 Appendix 1 Schedule of Works.\\\\r\\r\r
Any contractor wishing to be considered for appointment onto this framework agreement must complete and return the PAS 91 prequalification questionnaire. Responses to the prequalification questionnaire will be used to draw up a restricted list of companies invited to participate further in the procurement process. The number of companies to be invited to tender as a result of this opportunity notice will be restricted to a minimum of 5 and maximum of 7 suppliers (this will only be exceeded where multiple suppliers have the same total score) with a total of up to 5 suppliers appointed to the framework contract.\\\\r\\r\r
The Council is utilising an electronic tendering tool to manage this procurement and communicate with suppliers.  Accordingly, there will be no hard copy documents issued to bidders and all communications with the Council, including the submission of Supplier Responses, will be conducted via the ProContract system, which can be accessed using the following link:	\\\\r\\r\r
http://sebp.due-north.com\\\\r\\r\r
\\\\r\\r\r
For the information of Tenderers, advice on accessing the system is available using the following link: https://supplierhelp.due-north.com   \\\\r\\r\r
If you need further assistance using the ProContract system please contact the PROACTIS support team or Email ProContractSuppliers@proactis.com OR log a support call directly using the following link: http://proactis.kayako.com/procontractv3/Core/Default/Index \\\\r\\r\r
Please note expressions of interest must be registered before 11:00:00 Monday 13 May 2019. \\\\r\\r\r
Completed prequalification questionnaires and supporting information should be returned no later than 12:00:00 on Monday 13 May 2019.

title: INVITATION TO TENDER FOR THE OPERATION AND MANAGEMENT OF BASINGSTOKE MARKET
description:
Located in North Hampshire, the borough of Basingstoke and Deane has a population of 185,200 whilst the town of Basingstoke has a population of 117,200. Basingstoke's town centre is made of up of three main shopping areas: Festival Place, The Malls and the Top of The Town, the historic quarter and home of the twice-weekly market. The town remains a key regional retail and leisure destination with footfall in Festival Place exceeding 20 million visitors per year.\\r\r
\\r\r
As part of its work on improving Basingstoke's town centre and enhancing the local offer, increasing footfall and creating vibrancy, Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council (the council) is looking to appoint a market operator to manage the twice-weekly local market taking place on Wednesdays and Saturdays in Market Place in the Top of the Town area of Basingstoke.\\r\r
\\r\r
The market is an important part of the offering in the Top of the Town and has the potential to be a major element in driving footfall to the town centre and supporting the wider economic health of the area.\\r\r
\\r\r
The council is looking for an operator who has a strong track record of delivering successful markets and who can also demonstrate innovation and creativity in diversifying the offer, supporting local producers and makers and encouraging business start-ups.\\r\r
\\r\r
This contract will be for three years with an option for a further one-year extension and is expected to commence on Wednesday 1st January 2025.

title: INVITATION TO TENDER FOR THE PROVISION OF TREE MAINTENANCE SERVICES
description:
Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council (the council) is committed to maintaining and enhancing the boroughs built and natural environment.  Protecting and improving the attractive environment that residents enjoy is important; Basingstoke's trees provide an enormous asset and make it one of the greener towns in the south.\r
\r
The council is seeking to appoint a contractor to provide a tree maintenance service throughout the year across the borough of Basingstoke & Deane. The contractor will work closely with the councils in-house tree inspectors who will be identifying and issuing orders for the tree works. Works will include mostly pruning and felling, although there will be an element of tree planting and associated young tree care. The contractor will also be responsible for providing a 24 hour/365 day emergency call out service\r
\r
The contract will be for a period of 5 years commencing 4 October 2018 with the option to extend annually for up to a further total period of 2 years.\r
\r
The tree maintenance budget may be subject to variation year on year, but it is predicted to be between 1.3 million and 1.6 million over the 5 year period.\r
\r
The outcome of the procurement needs to reflect a theme that underpins the council's priorities to ensure the use of technology to improve customer access, speed up processes and enter into service delivery arrangements that improve service and reduce cost.\r
The Council is utilising an electronic tendering tool to manage this procurement and communicate with Tenderers.  Accordingly, there will be no hard copy documents issued to Tenderers and all communications with the Council, including the submission of Tenderers' Responses, will be conducted via the ProContract system, which can be accessed using the following link:	\r

title: INVITATION TO TENDER FOR A CONCESSIONARY PROVIDER AT BASINGSTOKE INDOOR TENNIS CENTRE AND STRATTON PARK TENNIS COURTS
description:
Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council ("the Council") are looking for an experienced, professional organisation (The Operator), to undertake the future delivery of Tennis at Basingstoke Indoor Tennis Centre, (consisting of four indoor and four outdoor tennis courts and the John Arlott Pavilion located in War Memorial Park), and the Tennis Courts located at Stratton Park. The successful tenderer will be provided an exclusive right to commercially operate and deliver tennis at these facilities on the basis of a concessionary contract arrangement. The operator will gain the right to exploit these facilities through payment, so as to allow them to run the facilities and operate a profit; a set percentage of which shall be shared to the Council. By nature of a concessionary contract tenderers must be aware that operational risk of an economic nature will be borne by the tenderer and no cost will be provided by the Council.\r
\r
Occupation and use of the facilities will be granted to the successful tenderer rent, free by way of lease from The Council as owner.\r
The purpose of this tender is to identify one successful operator who can develop and grow tennis provision at the facilities and give users the chance to learn and improve from a varied programme of coaching courses and pay to play opportunities.\r
The successful operator will be required to manage the facility, and deliver operational activities, through a delivery plan which demonstrates how they will approach the operational long-term goals, introduce best practice standards, and provide increased interest with positive outcomes, creating the best possible tennis facility.\r
\r
The tennis provision must be of the highest professional quality and delivery standards, providing a community focused programme, to maximise the potential capacity of the courts at both the Basingstoke Indoor Tennis Centre and Stratton Park Tennis Courts.\r
\r
The contract will be for ten (10) years, with an option for the council to extend the contract for a further five (5) years subject to performance and review.

title: DBOM TENDER FOR A NEW BASINGSTOKE LEISURE CENTRE
description:
Opportunity should be accessed via ProContract https://procontract.due-north.com/Register project ID DN749514.\r
Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council ('the Authority') is commencing a Competitive Dialogue procedure to find a leisure specialist partner to deliver a new water and leisure complex in Basingstoke.\r
\r
The contract opportunity is for the award of the BDBC Leisure DBOM Contract (the Contract) which comprises the following leisure centres: \r
- Design and build a replacement Facility for the Aquadrome\r
- Aquadrome current facility operation, until transfer of service to the new Facility\r
- Tadley Health and Fitness Centre operation\r
- Basingstoke Golf Centre operation\r
\r
Following previous consultation, facilities at the new complex should include a 25-metre eight-lane competition pool, 20-metre four-lane teaching pool, leisure waters with flumes, a 150-station gym, three studios and a spin studio, an indoor clip and climb or similar adventure-style activity, indoor adventure soft play, party rooms and café.\r
\r
Leisure specialists are being invited to submit first stage Selection Questionnaire (SQ) responses for the scheme. Following detailed dialogue work with short-listed suppliers that demonstrate the relevant interest, experience, and capability to deliver the project, it is anticipated that a preferred partner would be identified, approved by the Authority and awarded the final contract in May 2026.\r
\r
Detailed information on the overall scheme, including programmes; specifications and response documents are available to access once registered and expression of interest confirmed on ProContract.\r
\r
The Authority is utilising an electronic tendering tool to manage this procurement and communicate with Tenderers.  Accordingly, there will be no hard copy documents issued to Tenderers and all communications with the Authority, including the submission of Tenderers' Responses, will be conducted via the ProContract system, which can be accessed using the following link:	\r
https://procontract.due-north.com/Register \r
\r
Please note expressions of interest must be registered before 11:00:00 Friday 20th December 2024. After this time no new suppliers will be able to register and download the documentation on ProContract. This is to allow a locked time for bidders simply to review and upload the necessary response documents to ProContract prior to the SQ response deadline in an effort to reduce the likelihood of incomplete or late submissions.\r
Completed Selection Questionnaire (SQ) responses and supporting information should be returned before 12:00:00 (midday) on Friday 20th December 2024.\r
\r
Please remember that you must complete and submit your SQ response BEFORE THE SQ CLOSING DATE listed above.

title: Professional Consultancy Services for the Enterprise M3 Local Enterprise
description:
This is award notice is published on behalf of The Enterprise M3 Local Enterprise Partnership.

Enterprise M3 Local Enterprise Partnership's are appointing a Professional Consultancy Services for the Enterprise M3 Local Enterprise Partnership's multi-site Enterprise Zone, in Hampshire and Surrey & have been supplied with the attached documents.

Enterprise M3 Local Enterprise Partnership (LEP) established a multi-site Enterprise Zone in April 2017 seeking to deliver 10,000 jobs and support 131 businesses. The Zone relates to three sites covering around 40 hectares in Hampshire and Surrey: 

i.	'Basing View' in Basingstoke, Hampshire; 
ii.	'Longcross Park' in Chertsey, Surrey and, 
iii.	Whitehill & Bordon in Hampshire. 

An initial 5-year Implementation Plan was developed and undertaken between 2017- 2022. Over £24 million of investment has delivered new infrastructure and enabled site development at each of the three Zone sites. With the completion of this initial investment period, Enterprise M3 LEP is seeking to commission multi-disciplinary consultancy support that will take the zone to the next stage of delivery and support partners in maximising the jobs, economic growth and business rates retained income over the remaining 20 years of EZ status.

The objective of the commission is to provide information and documentation that will inform and support the development of the second Implementation Plan that reflects the long-term objectives for the three sites, the key partners and the LEP.

This information will provide an evidence base for additional investment required across the multi-site Enterprise Zone. 

Since the information and Implementation Plan will be jointly owned by all parties engaged in this programme (Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council, East Hampshire District Council and Runnymede Borough Council) it will be essential for the Service Provider to engage fully with these parties throughout the contract period.

title: Strategic Flood Risk Assessment and Outline Water Cycle Study
description:
The Basingstoke and Deane Local Plan 2011-2029 (ALP) was adopted in May 2016. The council has now undertaken a review of the plan and is due to progress an update to the Plan focusing on strategic issues, in line with national policy and guidance. An up-to-date SFRA and WCS will provide evidence to support decision making relating to future development and inform the approach taken, ensuring that the scale and location of development proposed can be met without increasing flood risk and adversely impacting on the borough's water environment. It will also help to ensure that required infrastructure can be planned for and brought forward alongside new development, in a timely and phased manner.

The SFRA and WCS will need to comply with the national level planning policy requirements, as set out in the National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) and Planning Practice Guide (PPG) and best practice. Both documents will need to provide the evidence required to facilitate the delivery of sustainable growth to meet needs, allow longer term planning to take place, enable key stakeholders to coordinate their work and ensure that opportunities to protect and improve the water environment and reduce flood risk are identified. The studies also need to be responsive to the flood and water issues and policy context which is particular to Basingstoke and Deane.
